insights.insight: The protocol has verified $1.1M in real GMV across 17,876 receipts — each one a cryptographically confirmed transaction, not a modeled intent signal. For marketers paying $5+ CPM on probabilistic targeting, this is the cost-per-confirmation benchmark to watch.

insights.topic: DKIM vendor expansion into AI and digital platforms
insights.insight: Ten new receipt-issuing vendors were added in a single overnight event, including Amazon, Stripe, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gumroad — extending verifiable purchase data beyond physical retail into software, subscriptions, and AI services for the first time. This is a supply-side category unlock, not a volume event.

insights.topic: Throughput deceleration is structural, not cyclical
insights.insight: 7-day GMV has contracted 64.8% from its $210,912 peak on April 13 to $74,367 today, and token acceleration has now posted two consecutive sub-1.0x readings — the protocol's own math confirms self-sustaining deceleration. Brands evaluating this as a high-growth network should weight current run-rate, not peak velocity.

insights.topic: Intraday receipt volume follows a predictable cycle
insights.insight: Across five consecutive days, receipt inflows peak consistently in the 16:15–20:15 window and trough at the 00:15–00:35 rolloff — a stable, repeatable pattern that has direct implications for optimizing campaign attribution timing against verified purchase events.

The May 2 heartbeat recorded a 23-CBSA single-event burst at 100% diffusion — the largest in observation history — while the active metro count has pulled back from a peak of 29 to 19. Maximum single-event spread coexisting with metro count contraction suggests geographic breadth is near ceiling.

insights.topic: Lightning micropayment layer confirms real consumer participation
insights.insight: 257 Lightning payouts totaling 6.75M sats have been claimed at 130 sats per receipt, establishing that verified submitters are real, incentivized individuals — not scraped or synthetic data. For brands, this matters because the receipt corpus has a traceable human provenance layer.
